question: Should memory-core unconditionally reject existing dreaming markdown over 16 MiB, or should the bounded-reader change include a documented/operator-visible recovery path before merge?
rationale: The cap is a deliberate reliability boundary, but it changes behavior for user-managed Markdown that current releases permit dreaming to read without limit.

options.title: Accept the hard cap
options.body: Merge the 16 MiB rejection as the intended safety boundary and record that oversized Dream Diary or inline files must be reduced before dreaming can update them.

options.title: Add recovery guidance first
options.body: Keep the cap but add user-visible diagnostics or documentation that explains how to identify and reduce the oversized managed file.

options.title: Rework the boundary
options.body: Pause the PR if maintainers want a different bounded behavior for large existing user-managed diary content rather than a hard rejection.

recommendation.title: Accept the hard cap
recommendation.body: Merge the 16 MiB rejection as the intended safety boundary and record that oversized Dream Diary or inline files must be reduced before dreaming can update them.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent storage-mode work is the closest available ownership signal for the inline and Dream Diary storage behavior.
